title: Contract-First Epistemology: Semester II — Return, Diagnostics, Transfer, and Production (Weeks 15–28)
object_of_study: Making evaluation durable: typed return, ledger reconciliation, seam analysis, diagnostics, domain transfer, critique, casepack production, defense, repair, and transmission.
main_question: What must return, reconcile, transfer and be defended before judgment becomes auditable?

claim_layers.claim: Governing Semester Question: What must return, reconcile, transfer, and be defended before judgment becomes auditable? (source-stated).

Instructional burden: make evaluation durable after Semester I has made evaluation possible; Weeks 15–28 begin with typed return and end with final casepack defense and method transmission (May 6, 2026, Course Architecture v1.0).

The course architecture is structurally declared (source-stated); classroom efficacy is a separate, not-yet-evaluable claim that the source itself says should not be asserted as proven until it returns through actual instruction, student artifacts, assessment records, and repair evidence.
The library registers Semester II as a distinct teaching witness that follows Semester I (REL-000005), not as a copy of the full course.
